usage_notes.note_text: Use the plural expectations in this standard interview phrase.
Informal in tone but neutral as a description.
Casual describes a noun; casually is the adverb.
A stakeholder can be affected by a project without owning company shares.
Informal; takeaway is common in British English.
As a noun use take-out; the verb phrase is take out.
Brainstorm can take a direct object; brainstorm about is often unnecessary.
Common in American English; starter is common in British English.
An appetizer comes before the main course, not after it.
Say go through security, not pass from security.
Neutral; reception is a common synonym.
Front desk names the service area, not the desk in a guest room.
Small talk is uncountable; do not say a small talk for one conversation.
Menu refers to the list, not usually the individual meal ordered.
Use catch up as the verb; catch-up is the noun or adjective.
Use follow-up for the noun or adjective and follow up for the verb.
Use follow-up for the noun and follow up for the verb.
Use a reservation for the booking and reserve for the verb.
The common plurals are syllabuses and syllabi.
A group project is collaborative; an individual project is completed alone.
Neutral; check is common in American restaurants.
Do not use receipt when asking how much you owe; the receipt comes after payment.
At an airport, a gate is a boarding area, not only a physical door.
Action items are specific tasks, not all topics discussed.
A cover letter supports a resume; it does not replace it.
Use check-out for the noun and check out for the verb.
Do not confuse a boarding pass with a ticket, which confirms the booking.
Agenda is singular in modern English; agendas is the plural.
A layover is between connecting flights, not the final destination.
A reference may mean the person or their recommendation; make the context clear.
Neutral; the exact greeting may be formal or informal.
Greeting is the noun; greet is the verb.
Assignment is countable; homework is usually uncountable.
You meet a deadline when on time and miss it when late.
Neutral; tipping customs vary by place.
A tip is extra money, while the bill is the amount charged.
Neutral; baggage is a common synonym.
Luggage is uncountable; say two pieces of luggage, not two luggages.
Qualifications are evidence of suitability, not only academic degrees.
Neutral to formal; goodbye is more conversational.
Farewell can sound formal, so use goodbye in casual speech when appropriate.
Use plans in the plural when asking generally about someone's weekend.
Office hours is normally plural even when referring to a recurring period.
Customs takes a singular verb when it names the government service.
Write key card as two words when it is a noun.
Use wake-up with a hyphen before call; wake up is the verb phrase.
Amenities are useful features, not basic room furniture in general.
Neutral; CV is used in many regions.
Resume without accents can also mean continue, so context matters.
Use reservation for the booking and reserve for the action.
Use by before a deadline time, not until when stating the required submission time.
A lecture is the teaching session, while a lecturer is the person.
